lines.trans: Wait—how come the two of you are walking in together?
I had met up with Seung-chan to watch a movie! You texted Seung-chan that Cindy was waiting here.
All bandaged up now.
Hey Manager, you are near the station, right? I am coming right down—hurry over!
Wait, leaving already? Did you not say you had something to tell Seung-chan?
Oh, it is nothing big—I made a bit of a mistake toward Producer Baek last time and felt I owed him an apology.
Since we are producer and cast member on the same show, I worried things might be awkward—I am sorry about back then.
Now that I have said everything I came to say, I will get going—goodbye.
Wait a second, Cindy! Take along that snack you said you liked last time!

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

가보다.gloss: to go and see; to visit

meanings.en: to go and check; to go see
meanings.note: Compound of 가다 ('to go') + 보다 ('to see/try').
Often used in past tense 가 봤다 for experiential meaning.

examples.trans: I'll have to go see for myself.
Have you ever been to Jeju Island?

meanings.note: Used as promissive polite (가져갈게요.).

examples.text: 이거 유출되면 안 되니까 일단 내가 가져갈게요.
examples.trans: Since this photo must never leak out, I will take the memory card with me for now.
Let us do that (will take it along) right away.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning 'together', often pronounced 가치.
Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.
Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: That is a really good idea.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: used before a verb to tell someone to stop an ongoing action

examples.trans: I'm so full I'll stop eating.

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I just arrived a moment ago.
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (껄끄러울).

examples.text: 같은 프로그램 피디랑 출연자인데 껄끄러울 것도 같고… 죄송했어요 그때.
examples.trans: Since we are producer and cast member on the same show, I worried things might be awkward—I am sorry about back then.
It is really uncomfortable, awkward compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.

meanings.note: Used as prospective adnominal (내려갈).

examples.text: 내 인생은 이제 내려갈 일밖에 안 남았어요. 겨우 스물셋인데 나 그동안 올라오기만 했어요.
examples.trans: Nothing remains in my life now except going downhill—I am barely twenty-three, yet all I have ever done is climb up.
Let us do that (going downhill) right away.

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Placed before the verb it modifies.
Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.

examples.text: 올해 우리 회사에 신입사원이 많이 들어왔어요.
examples.trans: Many new employees joined our company this year.

meanings.note: Compound of 들다 (enter) + 오다 (come)

meanings.en: to join (a company, school, or group)

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.
Short for 문자 메시지.

examples.trans: Why aren't you replying to my text?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: 방송 (broadcasting) + 국 (bureau/station)

examples.trans: I have to go to the TV station this afternoon.
Fans are waiting in front of the broadcasting station.

meanings.note: Often carries surprise
Used as compound noun (별거).

examples.text: 아 그거 뭐 별거 아니고 지난번에 피디님한테 좀 실수한 게 있어가지고 사과는 해야 될 것 같아서요.
examples.trans: Oh, it is nothing big—I made a bit of a mistake toward Producer Baek last time and felt I owed him an apology.
This point about anything major is really important.
I want to did you send? right now.
How about trying to did you send? together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 고령 군청에 사과 전화 다 했고요, 다음 주에 사과 자막 넣기로 했어요.
examples.trans: We already phoned the county office to apologize and agreed to air an apology caption next week.
Here the word for 'apology' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 그만 마셔, 너 그러다 실수할라!
examples.trans: Stop drinking now—keep going like that and you will slip up!
This expression comes from 'you might make a mistake!'.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.
Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.
Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close
dummy
Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: commonly used when urging someone to act

examples.trans: We're late, so let's leave right away.
Come inside quickly before you catch a cold.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.
Sino-Korean word.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: Oppa, do you have time right now?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Just a second, I'll be right there.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: What did you do last weekend?

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.note: Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.
We decided at the last meeting.
Did you hear about this cast member?
I was busy today because of cast member.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
